51031457.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to EED (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The EED protein (residues 1–441) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) via amine coupling. The immobilization level was approximately 1000 response units (RU). The running buffer was HBS-EP+ (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20). Compounds were diluted in the running buffer and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 μM at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. The association phase lasted 120 s, followed by a 120 s dissociation phase. The chip was regenerated with 10 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2.0) for 30 s. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 Evaluation Software v3.0. The dissociation constant (K_D) was determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 18 caption: Figure 18. Chemical structures of 44–46 and binding mode of MAK683 within EED. (A) Chemical structures of 44 (MAK683), 45, and 46 (BR-001). (B) Binding mode of compound 44 (MAK683) (gold) within the H3K27me3 pocket of EED (in deep-salmon surface) of EED (blue-white cartoon); interacting residues are labeled and represented as sticks; intermolecular H-bonds are represented as dashed black lines (PDB 6YVJ). The dark arrow points to the EED surface facing the C7′ position of the dihydrobenzofuran ring of MAK683. *IC50 values of H3K27 trimethylation inhibition over 6 days in tumor cells.
